output.summary: KEP-667 proposes building support for the out-of-tree Azure cloud provider, including a well-tested cloud-controller-manager with feature parity to kube-controller-manager. It hosts the implementation in new Kubernetes repositories and sets up AzureDisk and AzureFile CSI driver projects as SIG Cloud Provider subprojects. Current status: implementable, alpha.
output.rationale: Azure clusters depend on in-tree cloud provider code, and the KEP tracks moving that functionality out of tree. The stated goal is that Kubernetes clusters running on Azure should run the cloud-controller-manager. The AzureFile and AzureDisk plugins also depend on the Azure cloud provider, so separate CSI driver repositories are proposed for them. Removal of in-tree code is explicitly out of scope and handled by a separate KEP.

alternatives.option: Removing in-tree Azure cloud provider code within this KEP
alternatives.why_not: Non-Goals state that removing in-tree Azure code is out of scope and falls under the KEP for removing in-tree providers.

evidence.quote: Build support for the out-of-tree Azure cloud provider. This involves a well-tested version of the cloud-controller-manager that has feature parity to the kube-controller-manager.

Non-Goals
- Removing in-tree Azure cloud provider code, this effort falls under the [KEP for removing in-tree providers]
Since AzureFile/AzureDisk are also depending on Azure cloud provider, three new projects would be setup
Those projects would be subprojects under [SIG Cloud Provider provider-azure]
